Getting started

Audience: someone who has not seen this port before and wants a board running TF-M. Followed top to bottom, this document builds and runs the full chain — bootloader, secure image, non-secure image — on an EK-RA8M2 or EK-RA6M5. Everything deeper is linked at the end.

Expect about an hour the first time, most of it tool installation.

1. What you are building

Three images, flashed to one part:

ImageWhat it is
bl2MCUboot. Verifies and chainloads the other two. Lives at the base of flash.
tfm_sThe secure image — TF-M itself plus the crypto, storage and attestation services.
tfm_nsThe non-secure application. Either the port's demo app or a test suite.

Two repositories:

RepositoryHolds
trusted-firmware-mThe TF-M fork. The RA ports live in platform/ext/target/renesas/<part>/.
fsp_cmakeThe e2 studio / RASC projects, the build scripts, and the design record.

RASC is the source of config truth. The TF-M build consumes the generated FSP projects; it does not fork them. Pin numbers, clock settings, the memory partitioning and the TrustZone boundaries all come from the e2 solution. See DESIGN.md §1.

2. Prerequisites

Versions below are the ones this port is built and tested with. Others may work; these are what the results in DECISIONS.md were produced on.

ToolVersionNotes
e2 studio + RASCwith FSP 6.7.0-beta0Required even for command-line builds — see §4
Arm GNU Toolchain13.2.rel1arm-none-eabi-gcc on PATH
IAR EWARM10.10.2Optional — only for the IAR trees
CMake4.1.1
Ninja1.13.1
Python3.13Needs imgtool's dependencies; TF-M installs them
J-LinkcurrentThe on-board debugger on both EK boards
Visual Studio Build Tools2019Only for PSA Arch builds — they compile a host tool with cl.exe (D083(DECISIONS.md))

Hardware: EK-RA8M2 or EK-RA6M5, and a USB cable to the on-board J-Link.

3. Clone

Keep paths short. Build directories under a deep path overrun Windows' path limit partway through the Mbed TLS clone and fail with Filename too long on 3rdparty/everest/..., which does not mention length.

cd C:\Users\<you>\Documents\GitHub

git clone https://github.com/renesas/trusted-firmware-m.git
git clone https://github.com/renesas/fsp_cmake.git

rem  Only needed for the test-suite builds in §7
git clone https://git.trustedfirmware.org/TF-M/tf-m-tests.git
git clone https://github.com/renesas/psa-arch-tests.git

The two port repositories track the same branch:

cd trusted-firmware-m && git checkout ra8m2_gen_6_7_TFM && cd ..
cd fsp_cmake        && git checkout ra8m2_gen_6_7_TFM && cd ..

The two test repositories are pinned rather than tracked. Neither follows a branch of this port, both move upstream, and these are the revisions the results in TEST_RESULTS.md were produced against:

cd tf-m-tests     && git checkout e0a433c              && cd ..
cd psa-arch-tests && git checkout renesas-ra-tfm-2.2.0 && cd ..

That psa-arch-tests URL is the Renesas fork, not ARM-software, and the tag carries the difference. The tag sits on branch dev-api-tfm-renesas-ra-v24.03 and is upstream v24.03_API1.6_CRYPTO_1.1.0 plus four things: the tgt_dev_apis_tfm_renesas_ra target the scripts select with PSA_API_TEST_TARGET=renesas_ra, a host-compiler fix in the target-config generator, deterministic ECDSA gated off because neither crypto engine implements it, and tf-m-tests' ten fetch_repo patches already applied. **A plain upstream clone has none of these.** Supplying PSA_ARCH_TESTS_PATH also makes TF-M skip the patch step without warning, which is why the patches are committed in the fork rather than left to git apply (D014(DECISIONS.md)).

You do not clone MCUboot or Mbed TLS. TF-M fetches both during the first configure. MCUBOOT_PATH defaults to DOWNLOAD. MBEDCRYPTO_PATH does not: with <PART>_FSP_MBEDTLS ON, which is the default, fsp_mbedtls.cmake FORCE-sets it to an overlay built from the secure e2 project's ra/arm/mbedtls, and that overlay clone is what hits the Windows path-length limit. The first build is therefore slower and needs network access.

4. Build the e2 solution first — this is not optional

The TF-M build reads two files that only an e2 studio build produces:

  • <project>/Debug/bsp_linker_info.h — the BSP_PARTITION_* addresses the whole memory map derives from
  • <project>/Debug/memory_regions.*

Regenerating the project in RASC is not enough. The project must be built.

  1. Open e2 studio, File → Import → Existing Projects into Workspace, and select the fsp_cmake folder. Import the solution for your part and all its sub-projects:

    PartSolutionSub-projects
    RA8M2ra8m2_gccra8m2_gcc_mcuboot, ra8m2_gcc_CPU0_secure, ra8m2_gcc_CPU0_nonsecure
    RA6M5ra6m5_gccra6m5_gcc_mcuboot, ra6m5_gcc_secure, ra6m5_gcc_nonsecure

  2. Build each sub-project (Project → Build All). Ignore the resulting .elf files; only the generated headers matter here.

  3. Confirm the file exists before going on:

    dir ra8m2_gcc_CPU0_secure\Debug\bsp_linker_info.h

    Missing means the e2 build did not complete, and every later step will fail in a way that does not point here.

5. Build the firmware

Each script builds BL2 + the secure image, installs the SPE interface into api_ns\, then builds the non-secure image against it. There is one script per part and toolchain:

cd C:\Users\<you>\Documents\GitHub\fsp_cmake

scripts\app_build_ra6m5_gcc.bat
scripts\app_build_iar.bat
scripts\app_build_ra8m2_gcc.bat
scripts\app_build_ra8m2_iar.bat

app_build_iar.bat carries no part in its name and is RA6M5's; the other three name theirs. Each takes an optional pair of build directories, and each default is the pair the matching launch in §6 flashes, so passing your own paths means cloning the launch as well:

PartToolchainSecure buildNon-secure build
RA6M5GNUtrusted-firmware-m\build_ra6m5_sce9trusted-firmware-m\build_ra6m5_sce9_ns
RA6M5IARtrusted-firmware-m\build_ra6m5_iartrusted-firmware-m\build_ra6m5_iar_ns
RA8M2GNUC:\b\m2gC:\b\m2gns
RA8M2IARC:\b\m2appC:\b\m2appns

The RA8M2 trees are under C:\b\ for the path-length reason in §3; the RA6M5 trees sit inside the TF-M clone, whose path is short enough to build in. Build directories are disposable; delete one to force a clean build.

The build type is per part and not interchangeable. RA6M5 builds Debug. RA8M2 GNU must build MinSizeRel, because GNU Debug comes out around 414 KB against a 294,400 B secure region, where RA6M5's region is 521,728 B and Debug uses 322,960 B of it. RA8M2 IAR builds Debug, which does fit there.

Read the output; do not only check the exit code. The install step runs the option-setting brick guard over bl2 and tfm_s, and it reports by printing.

Where the images land, with RA8M2 GNU as the example:

C:\b\m2g\bin\bl2.elf                   the bootloader  (flash THIS, see §6)
C:\b\m2g\bin\tfm_s_signed.bin          the secure image
C:\b\m2gns\bin\tfm_ns_signed.bin       the non-secure image

6. Flash and run

Program the TrustZone boundaries first — once per board

The boundaries live in the part, not in the firmware, so a new board needs this step before its first flash. Use the Renesas Device Partition Manager: in e2 studio, Run → Renesas Debug Tools.

The screen takes six fields, in KB, and the values differ per part. Each part guide lists them in the order the screen asks, with the address each one derives from:

PartValues
RA6M5RA6M5_SOLUTION.md
RA8M2RA8M2_SOLUTION.md

RDPM erases both code flash and data flash. Reflash all three images afterwards. The step repeats only if you change the layout, which is RECONFIGURING_THE_LAYOUT.md.

The launches

Use the e2 debug launch configurations. They already carry the correct addresses and the two safety settings below. In e2: Run → Debug Configurations…, pick one, Debug. Every launch for a part lives in one project, whichever image it flashes — RA6M5's in ra6m5_gcc_nonsecure/, RA8M2's in ra8m2_gcc_mcuboot/.

RunsRA6M5RA8M2
the application §5 buildsra6m5_TFM_sce9_{gcc,iar}ra8m2_TFM_app_{gcc,iar}
the application with software ciphersra6m5_TFM_swCrypto_gcc—
the regression suite, no interrupt testsra6m5_TFM_regression_{gcc,iar}—
the regression suite with FLIH interrupt testsra6m5_TFM_flih_gccra8m2_TFM_flih_{gcc,iar}
the same with SLIHra6m5_TFM_slih_{gcc,iar}—
FLIH at isolation 2 and 3ra6m5_TFM_flih_L{2,3}_{gcc,iar}ra8m2_TFM_flih_L{2,3}_{gcc,iar}
FLIH at isolation 1 on the IPC backendra6m5_TFM_flih_L1ipc_gccra8m2_TFM_flih_L1ipc_gcc
PSA Arch crypto, attestation, storagera6m5_TFM_test_{crypto,attestation,storage}_{gcc,iar}ra8m2_TFM_test_{crypto,attestation,storage}_{gcc,iar}
the MCUboot secondary-slot upgrade—ra8m2_TFM_update_{gcc,iar}

Nineteen launches for RA6M5 and seventeen for RA8M2. The gaps in the table are real: SLIH has never run above isolation 1 or on RA8M2 at all, and RA6M5 has no upgrade launch (KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md §3, §7).

Only the first row flashes what §5 builds. Every other launch names a build tree of its own — m5gflih, m2cry, m2att, m2sto and the rest — so running §5 and then one of them either flashes different images or fails on missing files. Build the tree the launch expects, which for the FLIH row is scripts\reg_build_gcc.bat C:\b\m2gflih C:\b\m2gflihns ra8m2 flih 1 SFN, or clone the launch onto a tree of your own with scripts\mk_level_launch.py, which rewrites the paths and forces setTZBoundaries false.

Two safety rules

Flash bl2.elf or bl2.hex — never bl2.bin. The option-setting words live in discrete segments that a flat binary cannot express; a .bin writes them at the wrong addresses and can brick the part. D002(DECISIONS.md), D065(DECISIONS.md).

setTZBoundaries must be false in every launch configuration. The debugger otherwise derives TrustZone boundaries from the launched project's symbols, and launched against BL2 it gets them wrong. On RA8M2 the key appears twice — ...arm.jlink. and ...arm.e2lite. — and e2 defaults the second to true. Set both.

e2lite is still true in five RA8M2 GCC launches — flih_gcc, update_gcc and the three test_*_gcc — inert while J-Link is selected, live the moment the probe is switched. DESIGN.md §7.2, D102(DECISIONS.md).

Also leave erase code flash and erase data flash enabled on connect. **A stale ITS/PS area survives a reflash** and makes the storage suites fail in ways that look like code faults.

Pre-flash verification — run on every new build

Two checks, and a clean .srec proves neither of them. One coalesced segment spanning the option memory is the failure that bricked both EK-RA6M4 boards: the linker gap-fills between the words and writes values nobody chose (D002(DECISIONS.md), D094(DECISIONS.md)).

Check one is that the option words sit in discrete segments. check_ofs.py runs during the build; run it again by hand on the image you are about to flash, with the arguments for the part, because the windows are per part and the guard reads only what it is given:

set READELF=arm-none-eabi-readelf
set GUARD=..\trusted-firmware-m\platform\ext\target\renesas\common\check_ofs.py

rem  RA6M5
python %GUARD% --ra6-default --max-word 0x10 --require-segments ^
  ..\trusted-firmware-m\build_ra6m5_sce9\bin\bl2.axf

rem  RA8M2
python %GUARD% --max-word 4 --require-segments ^
  --region 0x02c9f040:0x02c9f280 --region 0x12c9f4c0:0x12c9f680 ^
  --region 0x02e07600:0x02e07698 --region 0x02e17700:0x02e17924 ^
  --region 0x12e17780:0x12e17800 C:\b\m2g\bin\bl2.axf

A pass names every segment it found:

bl2.axf        OK - 3 discrete OFS segment(s): 0x0100A100(4B), 0x0100A200(4B), 0x0100A280(4B)
PASS: OFS is in discrete per-word segments within the given region(s).

Run RA6M5's arguments against an RA8M2 image and the guard prints CLEAN (no OFS segments) — a false negative that reads as verification. --require-segments turns it into a failure instead, which is why it is above: bl2 is the image that carries the words, so an empty result is wrong by itself (D056(DECISIONS.md)). The check works under both toolchains, because it reads program headers and ILINK emits those like any other linker.

Check two is that the words hold the expected values. Dump them by address rather than by section name: ILINK renames the sections to P1, P7, P11, so -j .option_setting_* dumps nothing and prints no error against an IAR image.

rem  RA6M5
arm-none-eabi-objdump -s --start-address=0x0100a100 --stop-address=0x0100a2d0 bl2.axf

rem  RA8M2
arm-none-eabi-objdump -s --start-address=0x02c9f040 --stop-address=0x02c9f280 bl2.axf

objdump -s prints bytes in memory order, so each word reads reversed from its register value. Both toolchains produce these bytes:

PartAddressWordBytes as dumped
RA6M50x0100A100OFS0ffffffff
RA6M50x0100A200OFS1_SECfffdffff
RA6M50x0100A280OFS1_SELf8f8ffff
RA8M20x02C9F040OFS0ffffffff
RA8M20x02C9F044OFS2efffffff
RA8M20x02C9F0C0OFS1_SECfffffffd
RA8M20x02C9F0C4OFS3_SECffffffff
RA8M20x02C9F120OFS1_SEL00000000
RA8M20x02C9F124OFS3_SEL00000000

The count is part of the check. RA6M5 carries three words and RA8M2 six, so checking an RA8M2 image against RA6M5's three addresses finds nothing and fails a good image.

Then:

  • Flash bl2.elf or bl2.hex, never bl2.bin (above).
  • Re-read the RTT addresses for the image you are flashing. They move on every relink and differ per toolchain for the same source on the same part. Nothing in the launch carries them, so a wrong address is a silent "prints nothing", not an error. There is no table of them in this repository; any such table is wrong within one rebuild.
  • First flash on an unfamiliar board: consider -D<PART>_BL2_HALT_AT_MAIN=ON, which spins BL2 at main() so option/lifecycle registers can be read back before MCUboot runs. Read DLMMON for the lifecycle state. The address is per part: 0x400E002C on RA6M5, 0x40204038 on RA8M2 (R_PSCU->DLMMON; the register sits at offset 0x2C of R_PSCU on RA6M5 and 0x38 on RA8M2, and the two R_PSCU bases differ as well). Reading RA6M5's address on RA8M2 returns an unrelated register, not an error. **Do not read FAWMON/FSPR**: both live parts report BSP_FEATURE_FLASH_SUPPORTS_ACCESS_WINDOW = 0, so those registers are not implemented and the values are meaningless (D094 made the same point for RA6M4). The image is not bootable with it set, and it does not help capture BL2's log — the spin is at bl2_main.c:112-125, before any init or logging.

Seeing the output

Console output goes over SEGGER RTT, not a UART. Each image has its own control block and the address moves on every rebuild, so read it rather than reusing a remembered value:

arm-none-eabi-nm C:\b\m2appns\bin\tfm_ns.axf | findstr " _SEGGER_RTT$"

Point J-Link RTT Viewer at that address.

BL2's log needs a halt. BL2 and the secure image share RAM, so the secure image's startup wipes BL2's control block microseconds after the chainload; a viewer that auto-detects after reset always finds the secure image's. To capture BL2: breakpoint inside it, attach the viewer at BL2's address while halted, then run. D100(DECISIONS.md), D110(DECISIONS.md).

What a good run looks like

[INF] Starting bootloader
[INF] Bootloader chainload address offset: 0x68000
[INF] Image version: v2.2.0
Booting TF-M v2.2.0+...
[Sec Thread] Secure image initializing!
TF-M isolation level is: 0x00000001
[INF][Crypto] Init HW accelerator... complete.
Non-Secure system starting...

7. Test-suite builds

These use a different configuration from the application build — larger profile, isolation level 3, the IPC backend — so they are separate scripts and separate build trees.

rem  PSA Arch. One secure image serves all three suites; each suite gets its own NS app.
rem  The third argument selects the part; omit it for RA6M5.
rem  vs_build.bat takes a build directory; with no argument it only self-checks and exits,
rem  and it runs under setlocal so no environment would reach the next line anyway.
rem  psa_arch_ns.bat calls vcvars64 itself, so the two lines below are sufficient.
scripts\psa_arch_spe.bat  C:\b\m2cry   CRYPTO ra8m2
scripts\psa_arch_ns.bat   C:\b\m2cryns C:\b\m2cry\api_ns CRYPTO

rem  Regression suites (tf-m-tests). Fourth argument picks the IRQ suite.
scripts\reg_build_iar.bat C:\b\m2iflih C:\b\m2iflihns ra8m2 flih

Suites: CRYPTO, INITIAL_ATTESTATION, STORAGE, PROTECTED_STORAGE, INTERNAL_TRUSTED_STORAGE.

scripts\vs_build.bat must run first for PSA Arch — those builds compile a host tool with cl.exe. Without it you get C1083: stdio.h and nothing explaining why.

Full detail, build-tree naming and the RTT guidance: scripts/README.md.

8. When it does not work

TROUBLESHOOTING.md is indexed by symptom. The ones most likely to hit you on a first build:

SymptomCause
bsp_linker_info.h: No such file§4 — the e2 solution was not built
Filename too long on 3rdparty/everest/...build directory path too deep; use C:\b\
C1083: stdio.h in a PSA Arch buildscripts\vs_build.bat not run
INVALID CONFIG: TFM_SPM_DEBUG_TRACE AND ... _SILENCEAny non-Debug build type, given the platform's TFM_SPM_DEBUG_TRACE ON. MinSizeRel and Release set TFM_SPM_LOG_LEVEL to _SILENCE, the platform config then turns TFM_SPM_DEBUG_TRACE ON, and check_config.cmake:119 rejects the pair. Pass -DTFM_SPM_LOG_LEVEL=TFM_SPM_LOG_LEVEL_DEBUG, or -DTFM_SPM_DEBUG_TRACE=OFF for the smaller image
Nothing on RTTwrong control-block address (it moves every build), or BL2 — see §6
region CODE_RAM overflowedsee CONFIGURATION.md
